questionText: Suppose a binary search tree with 1000 distinct elements is also a complete binary tree. The tree is stored using the array representation of binary heap trees. Assuming that the array indices start with 0, the $3^{\text{rd}}$ largest element of the tree is stored at index __________.
explanation:
Step 1: Understand Array Representation of Complete Binary Tree
For 0-based indexing, the left child of node at index $i$ is at $2i + 1$, and the right child is at $2i + 2$.
The tree has $N = 1000$ elements, stored at array indices $0$ to $999$.

Step 2: Trace the Rightmost Path (Largest Elements)
In a Binary Search Tree (BST), larger elements reside in the right subtrees. Starting from the root (index 0), we follow the right children:
• Root: $0$
• Right child of $0$: $2(0) + 2 = 2$
• Right child of $2$: $2(2) + 2 = 6$
• Right child of $6$: $2(6) + 2 = 14$
• Right child of $14$: $2(14) + 2 = 30$
• Right child of $30$: $2(30) + 2 = 62$
• Right child of $62$: $2(62) + 2 = 126$
• Right child of $126$: $2(126) + 2 = 254$
• Right child of $254$: $2(254) + 2 = 510$

Node $510$ has no children because its left child would be at index $2(510) + 1 = 1021 > 999$.
Thus, node 510 is the rightmost leaf of the BST and holds the $1^{\text{st}}$ largest element.

Step 3: Determine $2^{\text{nd}}$ and $3^{\text{rd}}$ Largest Elements
• Node $254$ is the parent of node $510$.
• The left child of node $254$ is at index $2(254) + 1 = 509$.
• Node $509$ is a leaf node since $2(509) + 1 = 1019 > 999$.

Within the subtree rooted at node $254$:
• $V_{509} < V_{254} < V_{510}$

All other nodes in the tree lie in the left subtrees of ancestors of $254$, so their values are strictly smaller than $V_{509}$.

Therefore, the three largest elements are:
• $1^{\text{st}}$ largest element is at index 510
• $2^{\text{nd}}$ largest element is at index 254
• $3^{\text{rd}}$ largest element is at index 509
